profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, who had previously built companies acquired by IXC Communications. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company opened what it described as the largest data center in Texas in Carrollton in 2012, the anchor of the Dallas Fort Worth cluster that this registry row is part of, alongside CyrusOne buildings in nearby Allen, Lewisville, and Collin County. CyrusOne also operates a substantial San Antonio campus and an Austin facility, both long-running Texas markets for the company, though no specific acquisition or opening story for San Antonio or Austin individually was located in available sourcing this session. The company was acquired by ABRY Partners in 2007, purchased by Cincinnati Bell for 525 million dollars in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Lewisville, TX (DFW2) in Lewisville, Texas, publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 200,000 square feet of technical space, operated by CyrusOne.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 1200 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 300 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

CyrusOne Lewisville, TX (DFW2) holds 6 published certifications: PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), HIPAA (handling of protected health information), ISO 27001 (a certified information security management system), FISMA (a specific compliance or security standard), SSAE 16 Type II (a specific compliance or security standard), TIA-942 (a specific compliance or security standard). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Texas has 23 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 15 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 399.41 MW. CyrusOne Lewisville, TX (DFW2) contributes 12 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
